plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. This is because your payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so bidding your value ensures you win whenever profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losses. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value ensures I only win when profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid here since payment depends on others' bids, not mine. With a value of $18, I should bid exactly $18.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only that competing bid, ensuring non-negative profit. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily, while bidding above value risks losses. Since this holds regardless of others' bidding behavior, I will bid exactly my private value of $21 to maximize expected profit.
